court: High Court of Judicature at Madras
facts_of_case: Wife filed petition for divorce under Hindu Marriage Act. She claimed husband's petition was to harass her and she needed a transfer due to distance.

legal_principles.principle: A party's failure to appear in court despite service of notice can be taken as an admission of the averments made by the other party.
legal_principles.held: Despite service of notice to the respondent on 30.04.2021, the respondent has not chosen to appear before this Court either in person or through counsel duly instructed, which shows that the respondent/husband has nothing to deny the averments stated in the affidavit filed in support of the petition filed by the petitioner/wife for transfer of HMOP No.4 of 2021.

legal_principles.principle: A transfer petition can be allowed in the interest of justice, considering the facts and circumstances of the case.
legal_principles.held: Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, this Court is of the view that it would be in the interest of justice to give a fair opportunity to the petitioner.

outcome.final_order: Petition in HMOP No.4 of 2021 withdrawn and transferred to Family Court, Cuddalore.

keywords: Latin maxim: Nemo judex in causa sua
use_for_drafting: drafting a transfer petition for divorce
advising on jurisdictional issues in family courts
assisting with petitions under Section 13 of the Hindu Marriage Act
